items.context: Store each email as an individual JSON file in a deterministic directory structure (e.g. data/emails/{account_id}/{mailbox}/{uid}.json). Each file contains the full envelope (headers, body, attachments as base64 or external refs, IMAP UID, flags, labels). This gives you: (1) git-like diffability for mutations, (2) trivial Qdrant ingestion since each file maps 1:1 to a vector point, (3) filesystem-level backup/restore via cp/rsync, (4) easy agent-manager integration since agents read/write plain files. The IMAP sync daemon writes new files and updates existing ones; all triage mutations (label, archive, snooze) are JSON field updates on the file before a batch resync pushes changes back to the mail server.

items.context: Before any triage mutation (label change, archive, move, delete), copy the original JSON file to a shadow directory (data/emails/.pending/{account_id}/{uid}.json). Mutations are applied to the working copy. A periodic resync job diffs pending vs. original, pushes changes to IMAP, and on success moves the pending copy to a committed archive (data/emails/.history/{account_id}/{uid}/{timestamp}.json). On failure or user-initiated revert, restore from the original. This gives you: (1) full audit trail of every mutation, (2) safe batch revert before resync, (3) conflict detection if the upstream email changed between sync cycles. The resync step becomes a clear commit point - nothing touches the mail server until you explicitly flush.

items.context: Create a dedicated agent-manager profile (e.g. email-triage-reader) with path restrictions scoped to data/emails/ and read-only tool permissions. Tasks can be created like 'summarize unread emails from account X' or 'find all emails mentioning project Y'. The agent reads the JSON files directly - no custom API needed. For write operations (triage actions), create a separate email-triage-actor profile with write access to the email JSON files but restricted to the mutation schema (can update labels/flags/priority fields, cannot delete files). Agent-manager's existing approval workflow then gates destructive actions - an agent proposes triage changes as file diffs, a human reviews the diff, and only approved mutations get resynced to the mail server.

items.context: Run a lightweight file-watcher (fsnotify in Go) that monitors the data/emails/ directory. On file create/update, it reads the JSON, generates an embedding via Ollama, and upserts into Qdrant with the file path as the point ID. On file delete, it removes the corresponding vector. This decouples email storage from vector indexing - the email sync daemon does not need to know about Qdrant at all. Benefits: (1) Qdrant stays eventually consistent with the filesystem automatically, (2) re-indexing is just touch all files, (3) the same watcher can index attachments/summaries as separate vector points linked to the parent email ID.

items.context: Use IMAP UIDVALIDITY + highest-seen UID as checkpoint state (stored in a per-account sync_state.json). On each sync cycle: (1) check UIDVALIDITY - if changed, the mailbox was rebuilt and requires full resync, (2) FETCH all UIDs > last_seen_uid for new messages, (3) check FLAGS on existing UIDs for server-side changes (read/unread, moved). Use IMAP IDLE for real-time push when the server supports it, falling back to polling. Write each fetched email as a JSON file atomically (write to .tmp, rename). This avoids partial writes and gives you crash-safe incremental sync. Consider go-imap (github.com/emersion/go-imap) which has solid IDLE support and is well-maintained.

items.context: The current PRD lists mail-in-a-box as the only email backend, which is a significant adoption barrier. Since the sync daemon speaks IMAP/SMTP anyway, abstract the mail provider behind an interface with mail-in-a-box as just one implementation. The JSON-file storage model makes this natural - the sync daemon is the only component that touches IMAP, everything else works on files. This also de-risks the project: if mail-in-a-box has issues or the user already has Gmail/Outlook, they can still use email-triage by pointing it at any IMAP server. Provider-specific features (like Gmail labels via X-GM-LABELS extension) can be handled as optional enrichment on the JSON files.

items.context: The PRD specifies a full three-panel React dashboard, but with agent-manager integration, the core email triage workflow becomes: agent reads emails, proposes triage actions as file diffs, human reviews in agent-manager UI, approved changes resync. For v1, skip building a custom email UI entirely. Instead, provide a CLI for manual queries (email-triage search 'invoices from last week') and let agent-manager handle the review/approval UX. The agent-manager diff viewer already shows file changes clearly. This dramatically reduces scope while still delivering the core value (AI-powered email triage with human oversight). A dedicated dashboard can be a v2 feature once the file-based architecture proves out.
